nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let the pair list of $n$ be the list of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order. Let $b$ be a list of bits whose length equals the length of the pair list of $n$. For all $i < j < n$, the bit of the pair $(i, j)$ in $b$ is the entry of $b$ at the position of $(i, j)$ in the pair list of $n$.
nodes.title: Pair bits are read off by position

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from pairs of natural numbers to bits, and let $b$ be the list obtained by applying $f$ to each entry of the pair list of $n$ (the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$ in encoding order). Then for all $i < j < n$, the bit of the pair $(i, j)$ in $b$ is $f(i, j)$.
nodes.title: Pair bits computed by a function

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, CLIQUE accepts $x$ if and only if INDEPENDENT-SET accepts the image of $x$ under the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET instances.
nodes.title: Correctness of the complementing map from CLIQUE to INDEPENDENT-SET

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ with $m$ clauses is satisfiable if and only if Karp's graph of $\varphi$ has a clique of exactly $m$ vertices. Karp's graph has one vertex for each literal occurrence of $\varphi$, and two occurrences are adjacent when they lie in different clauses and are not complementary.
nodes.title: Karp's reduction from SAT to CLIQUE is correct

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph whose vertices are $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and let $k \le n$. Then $G$ has an independent set of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if $G$ has a vertex cover of exactly $n - k$ vertices.
nodes.title: Independent sets and vertex covers of complementary sizes

nodes.summary: For a mode and the Boolean saying whether a vertex $i$ is chosen, the result is true when $i$ alone settles the condition on every pair $\{i, j\}$: in the clique and independent-set modes it is true exactly when $i$ is not chosen, and in the vertex-cover mode exactly when $i$ is chosen.
nodes.title: Vertices that settle their pairs alone

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$, an input $x$ and a witness $w$ (bit lists), the verifier rejects if $x$ does not decode to a triple $(k, n, \mathit{bits})$. Otherwise it accepts if and only if $\mathit{bits}$ has one bit per pair $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$, $w$ has at least $n$ bits, exactly $k$ of the first $n$ bits of $w$ are set, and for every pair $(i, j)$, matched with its bit $b$ in the encoding order of the pairs, the pair…
nodes.title: The verifier for CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT-SET and VERTEX-COVER

nodes.summary: For every list $s$ of Booleans of length $\ell$, reading $s$ at the indices $0, 1, \dots, \ell - 1$ in turn (with default value false) gives back $s$.
nodes.title: Reading a list at every index

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with clauses $C_0, \dots, C_{m-1}$, let $i$ and $x$ be natural numbers and let $b$ be a Boolean. The triple $(i, x, b)$ belongs to the list of literal occurrences of $\varphi$ if and only if $i < m$ and the literal $(x, b)$ belongs to $C_i$.
nodes.title: Membership in the literal occurrences of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: A mode is one of three values, clique, independent set and vertex cover, naming the three graph problems CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT-SET and VERTEX-COVER that share one NP verifier.
nodes.title: Modes of the clique verifier

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$ and Booleans $b$, $s_i$, $s_j$, let $\mathrm{ok}_m(b, s_i, s_j)$ be the pair condition of $m$: $\lnot(s_i \land s_j) \lor b$ for clique, $\lnot(s_i \land s_j) \lor \lnot b$ for independent set and $\lnot b \lor s_i \lor s_j$ for vertex cover. Let $\mathrm{free}_m(s_i)$, the part that vertex $i$ alone settles, be $\lnot s_i$ for clique and independent set and $s_i$ for vertex cover, and let…
nodes.title: The pair condition splits by vertex

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$, the adjacency bit $b$ of a vertex pair $\{i, j\}$, and flags $s_i$, $s_j$ saying whether $i$ and $j$ are chosen, the pair condition $\mathrm{ok}_m(b, s_i, s_j)$ is $\lnot(s_i \land s_j) \lor b$ for clique, $\lnot(s_i \land s_j) \lor \lnot b$ for independent set, and $\lnot b \lor s_i \lor s_j$ for vertex cover.
nodes.title: Pair condition of the clique verifier

nodes.summary: For a Boolean $a$ and a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{\ell - 1})$ of Booleans, the chosen-flag pairs of the list $(a, s_0, \dots, s_{\ell - 1})$ are $(a, s_{\ell - 1}), (a, s_{\ell - 2}), \dots, (a, s_0)$, followed by the chosen-flag pairs of $s$.
nodes.title: Chosen-flag pairs of a list with a new head

nodes.summary: For a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{\ell - 1})$ of Booleans, the chosen-flag pairs of $s$ are the pairs $(s_i, s_j)$, one for each vertex pair $(i, j)$ with $i < j < \ell$, listed in the encoding order of the vertex pairs of $\ell$ vertices (rows $i$ ascending, within a row $j$ descending).
nodes.title: Chosen-flag pairs

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, write $P(m)$ for the list of pairs $(i, j)$ of natural numbers with $i < j < m$, ordered by $i$ ascending and, for each $i$, by $j$ descending. Then for every natural number $n$, $P(n + 1)$ is the list $(0, n), (0, n - 1), \dots, (0, 1)$ (empty when $n = 0$) followed by the pairs $(i + 1, j + 1)$ for the pairs $(i, j)$ of $P(n)$, in the order of $P(n)$.
nodes.title: Vertex pairs in encoding order for one more vertex

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$, the row-by-row check of a list of chosen-flags against a list $b$ of pair bits is defined by recursion on the flags. For the empty list it holds iff $b$ is empty. For a flag $a$ followed by the flags $r$ of the later vertices, write $\rho$ for the reverse of $r$: the check holds iff $|r| \le |b|$, either $a$ is free for $m$ or $\mathrm{sat}_m(b_t, \rho_t)$ holds for every $t < |r|$ (indices from…
nodes.title: The row-by-row check of the clique verifier

nodes.title: SAT decision on undecodable input (moved alias)

nodes.summary: For a mode $m$, a pair bit $b$ and a flag $s_j$ saying whether vertex $j$ is chosen, $\mathrm{sat}_m(b, s_j)$ is $\lnot s_j \lor b$ for clique, $\lnot s_j \lor \lnot b$ for independent set, and $\lnot b \lor s_j$ for vertex cover.
nodes.title: The pair condition left to the later vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $o_0, \dots, o_{m-1}$ be its literal occurrences (clause index, variable, polarity) in formula order. In Karp's graph of $\varphi$, the graph on $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ read off the clique pair bits of $\varphi$, vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if $i \ne j$ and the occurrences $o_i$ and $o_j$ are adjacent, that is, they lie in different clauses and are not…
nodes.title: Adjacency in Karp's clique graph

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $b$ be a list of bits whose length is the number of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < n$. Then the graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ read off the list obtained by negating every bit of $b$ is the complement of the graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ read off $b$.
nodes.title: Complementing the pair bits complements the graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
